content.text: What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Github pages

A sovereign digital commerce stack is a self-contained infrastructure that enables digital creators to sell products online without relying on third-party platforms like Stripe or PayPal. This setup ensures that creators retain control over their revenue, customer data, and product delivery, making it an attractive option for those facing restrictions or high fees on traditional platforms. By leveraging free hosting on GitHub Pages, creators can build a cost-effective and scalable solution that operates independently, without fear of platform downtime or fees.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture of a sovereign digital commerce stack on GitHub Pages is built around a few key components: GitHub Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. NOWPayments handles automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, charging a mere 0.5% fee. This setup allows creators to store and deliver digital products seamlessly, while maintaining full control over their infrastructure and revenue streams.
Who This Is Built For and Why

This infrastructure is designed for digital creators who want to sell ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, presets, beats, plugins, software, and other digital products without relying on Stripe, PayPal, or other payment processors. By building a sovereign digital commerce stack, creators can avoid platform fees, maintain control over their revenue and customer data, and focus on growing their business without worrying about platform restrictions or downtime.
A sovereign digital commerce stack on GitHub Pages ensures you retain control over your revenue, customer data, and product delivery.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The key components of a sovereign digital commerce stack on GitHub Pages include GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, Supabase or Google Sheets, Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, and NOWPayments. Each component plays a crucial role in enabling seamless digital product delivery, automatic order storage, and secure payment processing. By combining these components, creators can build a robust and scalable infrastructure that operates independently and efficiently.
How to Use This Knowledge to Deploy Today

To deploy a sovereign digital commerce stack on GitHub Pages, start by signing up for a GitHub account and setting up a new repository. Next, create a new GitHub Pages site and configure Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic. Then, set up Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. Finally, integrate NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification and configure your infrastructure for seamless digital product delivery and automatic order storage. Frequently Asked Questions
What is the cost of using NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification?
NOWPayments charges a mere 0.5% fee for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification, significantly lower than traditional payment processors like Gumroad (10% fee).
How do I store and deliver digital products using a sovereign digital commerce stack on GitHub Pages?

You can store and deliver digital products using Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery. This setup ensures seamless digital product delivery and automatic order storage.
Can I use a sovereign digital commerce stack on GitHub Pages for selling physical products?
No, a sovereign digital commerce stack on GitHub Pages is designed specifically for selling digital products, such as ebooks, courses, and software. It's not suitable for selling physical products.
What happens if my GitHub Pages site goes down or is unavailable?

While rare, downtime on GitHub Pages can occur. However, a well-designed sovereign digital commerce stack on GitHub Pages is built to mitigate such risks, ensuring minimal disruption to your business and customer experience.

Yes, you can integrate other payment processors with your sovereign digital commerce stack on GitHub Pages. However, be aware that integrating multiple payment processors can add complexity to your infrastructure and may require additional configuration and testing.
